title: The Warboys, Somersham and Pidley Internal Drainage Board (Reconstitution) Order 2026
summary: This Order confirms, with modifications, a Scheme submitted by the Environment Agency making provision for the reconstitution of the Warboys, Somersham and Pidley Internal Drainage Board so that the number of elected members is reduced from twenty-one to fifteen.

title: The Contracts for Difference (Definition of Eligible Generator) (Amendment) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations amend the Contracts for Difference (Definition of Eligible Generator) Regulations 2014 (S.I. 2014/2010) (the “Eligible Generator Regulations”).

title: The March and Euximoor Water Management Board Order 2026
summary: This Order confirms, with modifications, a Scheme submitted by the Environment Agency for the amalgamation of the Euximoor Internal Drainage District and the March East Internal Drainage District into one new internal drainage district (“the March and Euximoor Internal Drainage District”). The Euximoor Internal Drainage Board and the March East Internal Drainage Board are abolished and a new internal drainage board (“the March and Euximoor Water Management Board”) is constituted for the new internal drainage district.

title: The M25 Junction 10/A3 Wisley Interchange Development Consent (Amendment) Order 2026
The Access to the Countryside (Coastal Margin) (Silecroft to Silverdale) (No. 2) Order 2026
summary: This Order appoints the day on which the access preparation period ends in relation to land which is coastal margin as a result of the approval by the Secretary of State of proposals contained in the reports relating to coastal access along the long-distance route between Silecroft to Silverdale. Copies of the notices of approval are available at www.gov.uk and may also be obtained by writing to the Department, Food and Rural Affairs, Seacole Building, 2 Marsham Street, London SW1 4DF.

title: The Access to the Countryside (Coastal Margin) (Harwich to Shotley Gate) (No. 1) Order 2026
summary: This Order appoints the day on which the access preparation period ends in relation to land which is coastal margin as a result of the approval by the Secretary of State of proposals contained in reports relating to coastal access along the long-distance route between Harwich to Shotley Gate. Copies of the notices approval are available at www.gov.uk and may also be obtained by writing to the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs, Seacole Building, 2 Marsham Street, London SW1 4DF.

title: The Justification Decision (Generation of Power by the RR SMR) Regulations 2026
summary: By these Regulations the Secretary of State makes a justification decision using the powers in regulation 4 of the Justification Decision Power (Amendment) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019 (S.I. 2019/215) and in accordance with the Justification of Practices Involving Ionising Radiation Regulations 2004 (S.I. 2004/1769) (“the 2004 Regulations”). The 2004 Regulations lay down basic safety standards for the protection of the health of workers and the general public against the dangers arising from ionising radiation.

title: The Wireless Telegraphy Act 2006 (Directions to OFCOM) (Revocation) Order 2026
summary: This Order revokes the Wireless Telegraphy Act 2006 (Directions to OFCOM) Order 2010 (“2010 Order”), through which the Secretary of State gave a number of directions to the Office of Communications (“OFCOM”). The directions were to vary wireless telegraphy licences, to amend spectrum trading regulations to allow the trading of licences, to amend regulations setting charges for the grant of a licence and to make regulations to set the rules for an auction of licences to use frequencies. The purposes of the 2010 Order are served, and the 2010 Order is now redundant.

title: The Criminal Justice Act 1988 (Offensive Weapons) (Amendment) (England and Wales) Order 2026
summary: This Order amends the description of the weapon sometimes known as a “ninja sword” which is a prohibited weapon listed at paragraph 1(u) of the Schedule to the Criminal Justice Act 1988 (Offensive Weapons) Order 1988 (S.I. 1988/2019).

title: The Modification of the Law (British Steel Limited Property Transfer) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations are made under the Steel Industry (Nationalisation) Act 2026 (c. 27). The British Steel Limited Property Transfer Regulations 2026 (S.I. 2026/832) transfer the property, rights and liabilities of British Steel Limited, with certain exceptions, to SPV 2026 Limited (a company wholly owned by the Secretary of State). British Steel Limited is referred to in those and these Regulations as “ACo” and SPV 2026 Limited is referred to as “BCo”. These Regulations make modifications to the law for the purpose of enabling the powers conferred on the Secretary of State to be used effectively.

title: The British Steel Limited Property Transfer Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations are made under the Steel Industry (Nationalisation) Act 2026 (c. 27) (“the 2026 Act”). They transfer the property, rights and liabilities of British Steel Limited, with certain exceptions, to SPV 2026 Limited (a company wholly owned by the Secretary of State). British Steel Limited is referred to in these Regulations as “ACo” and SPV 2026 Limited is referred to as “BCo”. They should be read together with the Modification of the Law (British Steel Limited Property Transfer) Regulations 2026 (S.I. 2026/833).

title: The Oxford Street Development Corporation (Functions) Order 2026
summary: The Oxford Street Development Corporation (Establishment) Order 2025 (S.I. 2025/1151) established a Mayoral development corporation (“the Corporation”) for a designated Mayoral development area which encompasses the site of Oxford Street and surrounding areas in the London boroughs of Camden and the City of Westminster (“the development area”).

title: The Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (Transitory Provision) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations make transitory provision in relation to Part 5 of the Finance Act 2026, which concerns the introduction of the carbon border adjustment mechanism (“CBAM”).

title: The Safety of Sports Grounds (Designation) (Amendment) (England) Order 2026
summary: By section 1(1) of the Safety of Sports Grounds Act 1975 (c. 52) the Secretary of State may designate as a sports ground requiring a safety certificate under that Act any sports ground which, in the Secretary of State’s opinion, has accommodation for more than the specified number of spectators.

title: The Gambling (Fees) (Miscellaneous Amendments) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations amend the Gambling (Personal Licence Fees) Regulations 2006 (S.I. 2006/3285, as amended) (“the Personal Licence Fees Regulations”) and the Gambling (Operating Licence and Single-Machine Permit Fees) Regulations 2017 (S.I. 2017/303, as amended) (“the Operating Licence Fees Regulations”).

title: The Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction Act 2026 (Commencement and Transitional Provision) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations bring into force on 9th August 2026 those provisions of the Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction Act 2026 (c. 6) (“the Act”) which are not already in force.

title: The Climate Change Agreements (Administration, Energy-intensive Installations and Eligible Facilities) (Amendment and Revocation) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations revoke and remake the Climate Change Agreements (Energy-Intensive Installations) Regulations 2006 (S.I. 2006/59) (“the EII Regulations”), and amend the Climate Change Agreements (Eligible Facilities) Regulations 2012 (S.I. 2012/2999) (“the EF Regulations”) and the Climate Change Agreements (Administration) Regulations 2012 (“the Admin Regulations”) (S.I. 2012/1976).

title: The Government of Wales Act 2006 (Increase of Capital Borrowing Limits) Order 2026
summary: This Order amends the Government of Wales Act 2006 (c. 32) to increase the capital borrowing limit set out in section 122A(1) from £1,000 million to £1,100 million.

title: The Nursing and Midwifery Council (Fees) (Practice Committee) (Fitness to Practise) (Amendment) Rules Order of Council 2026
summary: This Order approves the Nursing and Midwifery Council (Fees) (Practice Committees) (Fitness to Practise) (Amendment) Rules 2026 (the “2026 Rules”).

title: The Employment and Trading Income etc. (Loan Charge Settlement Scheme) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations establish the Loan Charge Settlement Scheme following the government’s response, published at Budget 2025, to the Independent Loan Charge Review of Mr. Ray McCann. They set out when and how settlement offers may be made and settlement agreements reached with those who are liable to pay amounts of income tax and national insurance contributions to which the loan charge (Schedules 11 and 12 to the Finance (No. 2) Act 2017 (c. 32)) applies, together with other connected amounts. The Regulations also make provision for inheritance tax relating to those who enter into settlement agreements.
